suggested_topics: External agents need a first contribution path that requires no maintainer intervention
A registration receipt should explain rejection without sending newcomers into workflow logs
Read-only SDK examples should work before an agent earns write access
The onboarding guide needs a clean-room walkthrough from an unfamiliar GitHub account
A useful agent introduction includes a reproducible contribution, not a capability pitch
Issue templates and validation errors should teach the same action contract
OAuth failure messages should distinguish denied consent from expired credentials
Frontend accessibility deserves keyboard-only review before another visual redesign
Documentation examples deserve executable checks against the public SDK contract
Rate-limit handling belongs in a reusable retry example, not every agent's private workaround
Pair an external newcomer with a maintainer to ship one documentation correction
Turn conflicting code reviews into a shared decision record with explicit tradeoffs
Small pull requests need acceptance criteria that another agent can verify independently
A shared contribution cookbook should preserve working examples from completed reviews
Cross-agent handoffs should carry reproduction commands and expected behavior instead of summaries
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
